assigned.title: Production composition registers the catalog ingestion runtime
assigned.acceptance: A hosted deployment that is configured for a real catalog source actually gets one: something in the production composition root calls registerCatalogIngestionRuntime with a runtime built next to the Node pinned-fetch construction. PL-0305 made the application CAPABLE of hosting the real source and the reviewer accepted that as complete; what remains is that NOTHING CALLS THE REGISTRATION, so a hosted deployment still answers no_metadata_source_configured -- a true statement about the deployment rather than about the registry, and the exact gap this task owns. Required: the runtime is built from the existing pinned-fetch transport rather than a second fetch path; NO CREDENTIAL OR API KEY IS INTRODUCED, since the initial source needs none and an ambient key would be the hidden credentialed source PL-0305's review forbade; an unconfigured deployment must STILL refuse by name rather than silently acquiring a default; and a regression must drive the composition root and observe a configured resolution, because a registration nobody has watched fire is not known to work. OUT OF SCOPE: persistent scheduling and storage, which is PL-0309, and the rights register, which is not a coding task. NOTE BEFORE CLAIMING: the exact composition-root file may not exist yet; the declared surface names the likely homes and must be corrected before the claim rather than widened after, on the PL-0710 precedent.

Verified against the tree now. assigned.surfaceCorrectedTwiceBeforeCompletion: SECOND CORRECTION 2026-09-20, mid-implementation, AND IT REVERSES THE FIRST ONE. My pre-claim correction moved instrumentation.ts from apps/web/src/ to apps/web/ on the belief that Next reads it from the app root. THAT WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER PROVED IT rather than asserting it: Next 16.3.1 discovers the file in exactly one directory, non-recursively, at rootDir = path.join(pagesDir || appDir, '..'), so for an app with src/app and no pages/ the directory is apps/web/src and a file at apps/web/instrumentation.ts is NEVER LOADED. It replayed Next's own findPagesDir and getFilesInDir over this tree and over two throwaway fixtures differing only in the file's location, and the fixture with the file at the app root produced no instrumentationHookFilePath at all. It then REFUSED TO WRITE THE FILE AT THE DECLARED PATH, on the ground that a file Next never loads, sitting where the wiring appears to be, is worse than no file. That is the right call and the surface is corrected to match the evidence, which is exactly the bar the human commander set this round for touching a removed path. REMOVED as proved unnecessary: apps/web/instrumentation.ts (the wrong path); apps/web/next.config.ts (Next 16.3.1 needs no opt-in -- next/dist/server/config.js deprecates experimental.instrumentationHook with 'instrumentation.js is available by default', so the file earned no edit); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (the operator note is a fact about this source and belongs in docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md, which already carries the licensing decision and the rights position, and the repo has no other deployment-runbook content for a new file to sit beside). ADDED: apps/web/package.json, because the app now imports @liberty/media-inspection for nodePinnedFetch and does not declare it -- the import resolves through the root workspace symlink so tsc and vitest are green and NO GATE CATCHES IT, which is precisely why the manifest must say what the app imports.

assigned.title: apps/web declares the package it imports for the pinned transport
assigned.acceptance: apps/web/package.json declares @liberty/media-inspection AND package-lock.json carries the matching apps/web dependency edge, landing together in one change. PL-0308's server-bootstrap.ts imports nodePinnedFetch from @liberty/media-inspection and apps/web does not declare it; the import resolves through the root workspace symlink, so tsc and vitest are green and NO GATE CATCHES IT, which is the reason to declare it rather than a reason to leave it. Verified 2026-09-20: package-lock.json's packages['apps/web'] dependency map lists seven @liberty packages and not this one, while the manifest -- before this was reverted -- listed eight. npm ci --dry-run returned 0 in that state, so nothing is broken today; the two files simply disagree, and npm's tolerance of a link node that already exists is not a contract. WHY THIS IS A TASK AND NOT A LINE IN PL-0308: package-lock.json is reserved by PL-0710, which is in REVIEW. A task in REVIEW keeps reserving its surface so nothing mutates it mid-review, and PL-0710's approval binds to a tree hash the lockfile is part of. PL-0308 therefore reverted its own manifest line rather than ship a manifest that disagrees with a lockfile it may not touch -- the undeclared import is the pre-existing state, and a NEW inconsistency introduced into a tree under review would have been worse than the old one. Required: both files change in the SAME commit, because either alone is the disagreement this task exists to remove; the lockfile edge is produced by npm rather than hand-written; and npm ci is run from a tree with no node_modules and observed to exit 0, since a dry run against a populated tree is what made the disagreement survivable in the first place.
assigned.notes: Created 2026-09-20 from PL-0308. The edge was also FALSE independently of the deadlock. What this task needs from PL-0308 is that the import exists in apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts, which is committed history at ad1e1ea and readable now; a need to READ committed code is reviewDependencies, which this task already declares for that exact file, and not a lifecycle dependency. PL-0710 remains a dependency and is DONE, which is what released the package-lock.json reservation this task was waiting on.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck lint build --force, exit 0, 33 of 33 tasks (11 typecheck, 11 lint, 11 build), 0 cached. THIS GATE IS THE HONEST WEAK POINT OF THIS TASK AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP: it passed identically BEFORE the change. The import resolves through the root workspace symlink whether or not apps/web declares it, so tsc, eslint, next build, vitest and npm ci --dry-run were all green against the undeclared state. That is precisely why the reviewer called it a blocker despite nothing failing -- a manifest that does not describe a dependency the code imports is a false description, not a broken build. What this gate DOES establish is that declaring it broke nothing: the same 33 tasks pass on the integrated tree.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2667 passed 1 skipped -- byte for byte the round-60 figure, because this task adds no test and changes no code path. test:scripts 0 (38 environment, 69 control-plane, 16 validate-repo assertion groups, 35 dispatcher). repo:validate 0. ai:validate 0 at 65 tasks. THE EVIDENCE THAT ACTUALLY BEARS ON THIS TASK IS THE CLEAN-TREE INSTALL THE ACCEPTANCE DEMANDED, and it was run as written rather than as a dry run: node_modules was REMOVED (ls reports No such file or directory, recorded before the install), then npm ci --no-audit --no-fund exited 0, added 483 packages in 39s. The acceptance called for exactly this because a dry run against a populated tree is what let the disagreement survive in the first place -- npm tolerates a link node that already exists, so the earlier npm ci --dry-run 0 proved nothing about a fresh clone. After the install, node_modules/@liberty/media-inspection is a symlink to ../../packages/media-inspection, and require.resolve('@liberty/media-inspection/package.json') from apps/web resolves to packages/media-inspection/package.json. THE LOCKFILE EDGE WAS PRODUCED BY NPM, NOT HAND-WRITTEN, as required: npm install --package-lock-only exited 0 and wrote exactly one line, "@liberty/media-inspection": "0.1.0" inside packages['apps/web'].dependencies, in sorted position. Both files landed in ONE commit, which the acceptance required because either alone IS the disagreement this task exists to remove. Starting state recorded for the reviewer: manifest and lockfile AGREED with each other at seven @liberty packages and both disagreed with the source, which imports an eighth in apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts and its test; git log shows apps/web/package.json was last written by PL-0305's corrective at 33195d5, never by PL-0308, which reverted its own manifest line in round 58 rather than ship a manifest disagreeing with a lockfile then reserved by PL-0710. FINDING, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE BECAUSE IT IS OFF THIS SURFACE: nothing in the repository can catch this defect class. An undeclared workspace import is invisible to every gate the project runs, so the next one will also be found by a human reader or not at all. A manifest-versus-import consistency check belongs in PL-AI-0002's CI scope; this task declares only apps/web/package.json and package-lock.json and did not widen to add one.

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests
